gaps: Live testing requires the user's Home Assistant URL and Long-Lived Access Token.
Some Supervisor, HACS, radio, or custom-component operations vary by installation and must fail honestly when the capability is unavailable.
patterns: Use REST for common reads and mutations, then open a temporary WebSocket for subscriptions, richer registry/config flows, and post-action verification.
Reject ambiguous friendly names and require exact IDs instead of guessing.
All multi-entity mutations follow plan, apply, and verify stages.

novel_features.name: Verified household mode
novel_features.description: Preview a scene or script, run it, and verify every resulting entity state.
novel_features.rationale: Requires resolving registry metadata, comparing current state, applying service calls, and tracking live WebSocket outcomes as one operation.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent must change several household devices safely instead of firing an unverified scene or service call.

novel_features.name: Household exception check
novel_features.description: See open windows, unlocked locks, lights left on, low batteries, and unavailable safety devices in one answer.
novel_features.rationale: Requires domain-aware joins across states, device classes, rooms, devices, and labels rather than one API response.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for immediate household safety and comfort questions that span several entity domains.

novel_features.name: Routine incident explanation
novel_features.description: Reconstruct why an automation or script failed from traces, state changes, logbook entries, and errors.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a bounded time correlation across several records that Home Assistant exposes separately.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent needs evidence for one failed routine instead of dumping an opaque trace.

novel_features.name: Routine reference lint
novel_features.description: Find missing entities, unavailable services, disabled dependencies, ambiguous names, and stale routine references.
novel_features.rationale: Requires validating scene, script, and automation configuration against live registries and service catalogs.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before configuration changes or upgrades to catch deterministic breakage before Home Assistant executes a routine.

novel_features.name: Routine impact graph
novel_features.description: See every automation, script, scene, helper, and service target affected by changing one entity or routine.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a forward and reverse dependency graph built from synced configurations and registry identifiers.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before renaming, disabling, or removing something that other household routines may depend on.

novel_features.name: Mechanical household recap
novel_features.description: Review factual household activity, routine failures, presence changes, openings, and unavailable time for a recent period.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local SQLite aggregation across time-series history, logbook, traces, states, and registries without relying on an LLM.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for a compact, evidence-based household summary that remains useful offline.

novel_features.name: Health hotspot grouping
novel_features.description: Group recurring unavailable, stale, low-battery, and disconnecting entities into device, room, integration, and radio hotspots.
novel_features.rationale: Requires correlating live state, system health, registry ownership, radio metadata, and local availability history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when many entity symptoms may share one failing device, integration, room, or radio network.

novel_features.name: Standby energy finder
novel_features.description: Find devices drawing persistent power during explicit periods when related household states show inactivity.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local time-series correlation between power data and occupancy, media, light, and appliance states.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to turn household energy history into a short list of actionable standby loads.

narrative.headline: Safe household actions, offline memory, and evidence-backed answers on top of the full Home Assistant control surface.
narrative.value_prop: Match the useful breadth of hass-cli and ha-mcp, then add preview/apply/verify modes, routine debugging, reference linting, health hotspots, and household exception checks. The same typed Go command tree works for people, scripts, agents, and MCP clients.
narrative.auth_narrative: Set HASS_SERVER to your Home Assistant instance URL and HASS_TOKEN to a Long-Lived Access Token created from your Home Assistant profile. The CLI sends the token as a bearer credential to REST and as an access token during WebSocket authentication; it never prints or syncs the token.

quickstart.comment: Validate configuration and see the exact server/auth prerequisites without making a request.
Create a local household snapshot for offline search and compound commands.
Get a context-efficient answer to the most common whole-home question.
Preview every resolved target and expected action before changing the home.

troubleshoots.fix: Create a fresh Long-Lived Access Token in the Home Assistant profile and export it as HASS_TOKEN.
Set HASS_SERVER to a URL reachable from this machine, including port 8123 when required, then run home-assistant-pp-cli doctor.

troubleshoots.symptom: A friendly name matches multiple entities
troubleshoots.fix: Re-run with the exact entity_id returned in the ambiguity error; the CLI will not guess.

troubleshoots.symptom: A command reports that the installation lacks a capability
troubleshoots.fix: Run home-assistant-pp-cli system info --agent and use the reported stock Core, Supervisor, or integration-supported command path.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent needs to inspect or control a Home Assistant household, debug routines, maintain a self-hosted installation, or answer questions that span multiple entities and histories. It is especially useful when changes must be previewed, machine-readable, and verified rather than guessed from friendly names.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to control Apple's Home app or HomeKit devices that are not bridged into Home Assistant.
Do not use this CLI to bypass Home Assistant authentication or expose a private instance directly to the public internet.
Do not use destructive registry, restore, restart, or update commands without reviewing their dry-run or plan output.
Do not use local-only compound commands before syncing the required resources.
